themes: Turning from false worship to Allah
summary_for_children: An-Naml means The Ants. It tells of Sulayman, who heard an ant warn the others, of a hoopoe that brought news of the Queen of Sheba, and how she came to believe in Allah. It also tells briefly of Musa, Salih and Lut.
world_title: Valley of the Ants and the Glass Palace
environment_concept: A journey with Sulayman's story told from the land around it: the valley of the ants, the hoopoe's flight to Sheba, a throne that appears in a blink, and a palace whose floor looks like water.
architecture_and_scenery: A sunny valley with ant hills, cedar and stone, a kingdom of Sheba with sun-worshipping courtyards, and a palace floored with smooth glass over water.

palette.lighting: Warm golden valley light, then the cool reflective glow of the glass palace
palette.atmosphere: Busy valley sounds of insects and birds; a hushed palace

areas.name: Valley of the Ants
areas.description: Ant hills and tiny paths; the player walks carefully so as not to harm them.

areas.name: The Hoopoe's Perch
areas.description: An empty perch among the birds where the hoopoe should be.

areas.name: Road to Sheba
areas.description: A long road to a southern kingdom.

areas.name: The Glass Floor
areas.description: A palace floor of glass over water.

areas.name: Moving Mountains
areas.description: Distant mountains drifting like clouds: symbolic, at the world's edge.

activities.name: Find the hoopoe
activities.description: One branch on the birds' tree is empty. Follow the road and find the hoopoe, then read 27:20-22.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Match each place to its ayah
activities.description: Match each place in the valley to the ayah it comes from.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Walk with care
activities.description: Cross the valley of the ants without stepping on their trails, and talk about caring for small creatures.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Gratitude prayer
activities.description: Read 27:19 at the valley's end and talk about thanking Allah.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: Narration tells each scene from the ayahs. Sulayman, the Queen and all people are never shown or voiced; animals act only as the ayahs say.
learning_objectives: Retell the ant and the hoopoe
Explain that the Queen turned to Allah

status.playable_environment: first version built: its own valley (ant hills with ants, a tree of birds with an empty branch, a hoopoe to find, a far city, a glass floor over water, drifting mountains), a find-it activity in the scene and a matching game
status.testing: checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL at 1280x800; not tested on phones or real GPUs
status.tested_by: automated screenshots of the scene and tapping the hoopoe

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.
